title: Issue-detection invoke must require USE on the gateway secret it decrypts, not only UPDATE on the experiment
answers: Why can a user run issue detection with another user's AI Gateway API key?
issues/invoke secret_id authorization check for gateway secrets
Which permission is needed to use a gateway secret in issue detection?
body:
Symptom: a user with edit rights on their own experiment can run issue detection with another user's AI Gateway secret, so the server decrypts a key they cannot access.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_invoke_issue_detection previously was only validate_can_update_experiment, while the handler passes the body secret_id to _fetch_provider_credentials, which decrypts it via the tracking store's _get_decrypted_secret.
Fix pattern: keep the UPDATE check on the experiment, then read secret_id from the body and return _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use. Map INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION to this validator in BEFORE_REQUEST_VALIDATORS. The shared helper _get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id delegates to _get_gateway_secret_permission, so workspace resolution and the default-permission floor match the gateway secret RPCs.
Constraints: the falsy guard (if not secret_id) must match the handler's own `if secret_id:` check, so an empty or absent secret_id needs no grant while an explicit id is always checked. READ on the secret is not enough; unknown ids resolve to no grant and are denied. genai/evaluate/invoke and scorer/invoke take no secret_id and keep the experiment-only check. An endpoint_name on this route is NOT checked against gateway-endpoint permissions (known gap).
Applies: any basic-auth route whose handler decrypts or consumes a caller-supplied gateway secret id; applies to validators in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py.
applies: Basic-auth before-request validators for routes that cause the server to use a gateway secret from the request body.
says: Users can trigger issue detection by providing AI Gateway secrets they cannot access.
Require usage permissions on AI Gateway credentials when running automated issue detection.
Team members are consuming shared model provider API keys without granted permissions.
Issue detection jobs execute using private gateway secrets owned by other accounts.
Block unauthorized users from running trace issue analysis with restricted gateway keys.
search: The basic-auth route validator validate_can_invoke_issue_detection in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py must verify USE permission on the request secret_id alongside UPDATE permission on the experiment. The check calls _get_gateway_secret_permission via _get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id, requiring can_use for explicit secret_ids while allowing empty or absent ids. Unknown secret IDs are denied, READ permission is insufficient, endpoint_name is not checked against gateway-endpoint permissions, and genai/evaluate/invoke and scorer/invoke retain experiment-only checks. Applies to basic-auth routes whose handlers decrypt caller-supplied gateway secrets via _fetch_provider_credentials and tracking store _get_decrypted_secret.
